note: Linifanib reached CRC patients on Abbott's colon xenografts and VEGF-permeability mouse models but was never tested against placebo in CRC; the class's one placebo-controlled CRC win is famitinib's phase 2b PFS, and the two phase 3s (famitinib FACT, donafenib) finished in 2019-2020 and were never reported.
label: Colorectal (VEGFR multikinase)

engagement.confidence_note: model_filed is null for every entry: no member has a public regulator review (linifanib never reached an NDA; donafenib and famitinib are NMPA-reviewed, reviews not published), so whether this model was in the linifanib IND cannot be read.
engagement.judgement: Opens the engagement strip with Abbott's mechanism-based PD model (VEGF-induced vascular permeability), a different system and prediction from the tumour xenografts, so it gets its own track. No human readout existed in 2006.
engagement.model: VEGF-induced uterine edema in mice (vascular-permeability PD model, ABT-869/linifanib)
engagement.note: Linifanib blocked VEGF-induced vascular permeability (uterine edema ED50 0.5 mg/kg) and corneal angiogenesis in mice; no dosed-human readout yet.
engagement.short: Mouse VEGF permeability blocked; no human readout
engagement.quote: In vivo ABT-869 is effective orally in the mechanism-based murine models of VEGF-induced uterine edema (ED50 = 0.5 mg/kg) and corneal angiogenesis (>50% inhibition, 15 mg/kg).

engagement.magnitude_basis: mouse ED50 for permeability blockade (0.5 mg/kg) vs dose-dependent DCE-MRI permeability reduction in patients; the abstract gives no human effect size
engagement.population: Refractory solid malignancies, phase 1 (33 patients; one colon cancer partial response)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Wong 2009. Patients were a mixed solid-tumour phase 1 cohort, not CRC only (the brief admits healthy volunteers for engagement, so a mixed cohort is taken as admissible); the readout is an imaging surrogate of permeability, not the uterine-edema assay itself. Phase 1 NCT number not found, registry_date null.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me (Albert 2006 model, Wong 2009 trial); the trial paper does not put the mouse data beside its own. Scored same, downstream: the mouse model's quantity (VEGF-driven vascular permeability) fell dose-dependently on DCE-MRI in dosed patients. Circulating endothelial cells and plasma VEGF moved too but were not model readouts.
engagement.model: VEGF-induced uterine edema in mice (vascular-permeability PD model, ABT-869/linifanib)
engagement.note: Phase 1: DCE-MRI showed dose-dependent, exposure-correlated reduction in tumour vascular permeability, the quantity the mouse edema model predicted linifanib would block.
engagement.short: DCE-MRI permeability fell as mouse model said
engagement.quote: Dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) showed dose-dependent reduced tumor vascular permeability that correlated with drug exposure.
engagement.reason: DCE-MRI permeability fell as model said

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 21505059, epub 2011-04-19). JPET full text was not reachable (WebFetch 403, Firecrawl returned the page shell), so the SW620 Ktrans percentage, host strain and whether the paper cites the clinical DCE-MRI data are unverified. model_filed null: no member has a public regulator review.
engagement.judgement: Own track: a tumour vascular-function PD model (SW620 xenograft read by DCE-MRI Ktrans, microvessel density, pericyte coverage, hypoxia) is a different system with a different prediction from the draft's uterine-edema permeability assay (no tumour) and from the colon xenograft growth-inhibition track (Albert 2006, unnamed line, tumour volume). Retrodiction: the abstract itself says ABT-869 'has undergone phase I and II clinical trials', and the patient DCE-MRI permeability result was public in Wong 2009, two years before this model ran. Opening entry at first use is untested by the brief's dating rule and carries retrodiction false because lint forbids the flag on an untested entry; the retro entry that follows carries it. A checker who treats every human CRC cell-line xenograft as one system would fold this into crc-cellline-xenograft-mouse as an engagement entry instead.
engagement.model: SW620 colon carcinoma (and HT1080 fibrosarcoma) xenografts in mice read by DCE-MRI, microvessel density, pericyte coverage and hypoxia: tumour vascular-function PD model (ABT-869/linifanib 25 mg/kg/day)
engagement.note: SW620 colon xenografts: DCE-MRI permeability (Ktrans) and hypoxic fraction fell by day 4 of linifanib 25 mg/kg/day, as in HT1080 (>60%); run after phase 1.
engagement.quote: After 2 days of treatment on the HT1080 model, vascular permeability, K(trans), was reduced by >60% and hypoxic tumor fraction was significantly decreased, which was also seen in the SW620 tumors after 4 days of treatment.

engagement.magnitude_basis: mouse DCE-MRI Ktrans reduction (>60% in HT1080 at day 2, 'also seen' in SW620 at day 4, no SW620 percentage in the abstract) vs dose-dependent DCE-MRI permeability reduction in phase 1 patients, for which the Wong 2009 abstract gives no effect size
engagement.population: Refractory solid malignancies, phase 1 (33 patients; one colon cancer partial response); the same mixed cohort the draft's engagement cell already admits
engagement.confidence_note: Paired by me from two abstracts: Jiang 2011 (model, PMID 21505059) and Wong 2009 (patients, PMID 19720910, epub 2009-08-31). epub_year and print_year are those of the comparison date (the 2011 model paper), not of src, which is the earlier patient paper. Whether Jiang 2011 itself cites the clinical DCE-MRI result could not be checked (full text unreachable), so comparison_stated stays false. Phase 1 NCT number not found; registry_date null.
engagement.judgement: Scored retro, never same (decision 10): the clinic knew in 2009 that linifanib lowers tumour vascular permeability on DCE-MRI, and the SW620 xenograft reproduced that Ktrans drop in 2011. Direction only: the abstracts give no commensurable effect size. readout_tier downstream: Ktrans is vascular physiology downstream of VEGFR2 blockade, though here mouse and patient readouts are the same imaging quantity, which is closer than the draft's uterine-edema pairing. Year 2011 is the first date both sides were public.
engagement.model: SW620 colon carcinoma (and HT1080 fibrosarcoma) xenografts in mice read by DCE-MRI, microvessel density, pericyte coverage and hypoxia: tumour vascular-function PD model (ABT-869/linifanib 25 mg/kg/day)
engagement.note: Patients' DCE-MRI permeability fell dose-dependently (Wong 2009); the SW620 xenograft reproduced that Ktrans drop two years later, so the model is a retrodiction.
engagement.short: Xenograft Ktrans drop matches patient DCE-MRI
engagement.quote: Dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) showed dose-dependent reduced tumor vascular permeability that correlated with drug exposure.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Albert 2006; the colon line(s) used are not named in the abstract.
dose.judgement: Opening entry: the xenograft PK/PD analysis stated an explicit exposure target (plasma linifanib above 0.08 ug/mL for at least 7 h/day) before any human PK existed. No tolerability margin is stated, so margin_stated is false.
dose.model: Human tumour cell-line xenografts in mice incl. colon carcinoma (ABT-869/linifanib)
dose.note: Xenograft PK/PD set the target: efficacy tracked time above 0.08 ug/mL (protein-binding-corrected KDR IC50) for >=7 h/day, not AUC or Cmax; no human PK yet.
dose.quote: efficacy correlated more strongly with time over a threshold value (cellular KDR IC50 corrected for plasma protein binding = 0.08 microg/mL, >or=7 hours) than with plasma area under the curve or Cmax.

dose.magnitude_basis: my own steady-state estimate: 17.5 mg/day (0.25 mg/kg, the tolerated dose) over the reported mean oral clearance 2.7 L/h gives about 0.27 ug/mL average, above the 0.08 ug/mL threshold all day; no source states the ratio
dose.population: Refractory solid malignancies, phase 1; later CRC trials dosed 17.5 mg (monotherapy) or 7.5-12.5 mg (with mFOLFOX6)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the exposure comparison is my arithmetic from the abstract's mean clearance and nominal dose, not a stated or measured trough. Sufficiency is not shown for linifanib in CRC: the 2014 phase 2 used lower doses (7.5/12.5 mg) against an active comparator and the 17.5 mg KRAS-mutant phase 2 stopped for futility on ORR; the one placebo-controlled CRC win (famitinib) has no public exposure target. Phase 1 NCT not found.
dose.judgement: Scored same, low confidence, under 'reached': the model's exposure target was cleared at the tolerated phase 1 dose, with DCE-MRI permeability falling in step with exposure. Not contra via efficacy because neither linifanib CRC trial tested the model's actual prediction (activity versus no VEGF blockade): one was superiority over bevacizumab, the other a single-arm ORR gate. A checker who scores those trials as failures should turn this entry contra with derived_from efficacy.
dose.model: Human tumour cell-line xenografts in mice incl. colon carcinoma (ABT-869/linifanib)
dose.note: Phase 1 PK (clearance 2.7 L/h, half-life 18 h) puts the tolerated 0.25 mg/kg dose above the xenograft 0.08 ug/mL threshold all day; whether that was enough in CRC was never cleanly tested.
dose.short: Exposure target cleared at tolerated dose
dose.quote: Oral clearance of ABT-869 was linear, with a mean of 2.7 +/- 1.2 L/h and half-life of 18.4 +/- 5.7 hours, with no evidence of drug accumulation at day 15.
dose.reason: Target exposure reached; sufficiency untested in CRC

dose.confidence_note: Chinese-language article (Yao Xue Xue Bao 2014;49:1684-8, PMID 25920197, no DOI); English abstract only. The famitinib phase 1 (NCT01762280, 2009-06 to 2012-04; Zhou 2013, PMID 24043137) was complete and published before this model, so it is a retrodiction. model_filed null: famitinib has no public regulator review.
dose.judgement: Own track: an in-silico cross-species PK model is a different system from any animal track, and famitinib's own program has no public CRC animal model, so this is the one famitinib model that was ever compared with its patients. Opening entry at first use is untested by the dating rule and carries retrodiction false because lint forbids the flag on an untested entry; the retro entry that follows carries it, since the human PK it was checked against already existed.
dose.model: GastroPlus physiologically based pharmacokinetic models of famitinib in rat and monkey, scaled to predict human plasma exposure and tissue distribution (Yu 2014)
dose.note: GastroPlus rat and monkey PBPK models (AUC fit ratios 1.00, 0.97) scaled to predict human famitinib PK and tissue distribution; built after the phase 1.
dose.short: Rat/monkey PBPK predicts human famitinib PK
dose.quote: This study is to establish physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models of famitinib in rat and monkey, and then to predict the pharmacokinetics and tissue distribution of famitinib in human based on the PBPK models.

dose.magnitude_basis: observed/predicted human AUC0-inf ratio: 1.63 (rat-scaled model) and 1.57 (monkey-scaled model); the model under-predicted exposure by about 1.6-fold, inside the 2-fold band PBPK predictions are conventionally judged by
dose.population: Chinese patients with advanced solid tumours (famitinib phase 1, NCT01762280, 4-30 mg/day; 25 mg recommended) is the inferred observed dataset; the famitinib CRC phase 2b (NCT01762293) used the same 25 mg dose
dose.confidence_note: Abstract only, Chinese-language paper. The abstract does not name the human dataset; it is inferred to be the Zhou 2013 phase 1 (shared authors Chen XY and Zhong DF, Shanghai Institute of Materia Medica), so subjects is patients, not healthy volunteers. NCT01762280 has no posted results, registry_date null. The famitinib healthy-volunteer PK studies (NCT05046808 and the 2022-2023 DDI/food studies) post-date the model and were not compared with it.
dose.judgement: Scored retro, not same (decision 10): the model reproduced human exposure that was already measured, within 2-fold, and the source says so ('predicting pharmacokinetic of famitinib in human successfully'). This answers only the reached half of the dose question: the model sets no effective-exposure target and states no tolerability margin (margin_stated false), so sufficiency in CRC is untouched and the entry does not interact with the famitinib PFS win on the xenograft track. The first prospective use of the model (the abstract proposes DDI prediction) has no published patient comparison, so no further entry.
dose.model: GastroPlus physiologically based pharmacokinetic models of famitinib in rat and monkey, scaled to predict human plasma exposure and tissue distribution (Yu 2014)
dose.note: Observed/predicted human AUC0-inf was 1.63 (rat-scaled) and 1.57 (monkey-scaled): exposure reproduced within 2-fold; the model sets no efficacy target, so sufficiency is untouched.
dose.quote: The AUC0-∞, ratios of observed and predicted data in human were 1.63 (rat to human) and 1.57 (monkey to human), respectively.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the colon xenograft line is not named in the abstract.
efficacy.judgement: Model-first-use year for the track. No public CRC model exists for famitinib (Hengrui's preclinical data unpublished; the only famitinib xenograft paper is gastric, 2016) or donafenib (HCC papers only), so the class track is linifanib's xenograft and the other two members are scored against it as sibling drugs.
efficacy.model: Human tumour cell-line xenografts in mice incl. colon carcinoma (ABT-869/linifanib)
efficacy.note: Linifanib inhibited growth of colon and other carcinoma xenografts (ED50 1.5-5 mg/kg twice daily); no CRC patient result existed to compare.
efficacy.quote: In tumor growth studies, ABT-869 exhibits efficacy in human fibrosarcoma and breast, colon, and small cell lung carcinoma xenograft models (ED50 = 1.5-5 mg/kg, twice daily)

efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft tumour growth inhibition (ED50 1.5-5 mg/kg) vs placebo-controlled PFS hazard ratio 0.60; not commensurable
efficacy.population: Unselected, refractory mCRC after all standard therapies (third line and beyond)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Xu 2017; quote verbatim in the abstract. The pairing crosses drugs: the xenograft was dosed with linifanib and the trial drug is famitinib (sibling member, product_in_model false). NCT01762293 has no results posted, registry_date null; the result was first presented at ASCO-GI 2015 (conference abstract, not an admissible tier), hence year 2017. The same trial's secondary OS was null (7.4 vs 7.2 months, P = 0.657).
efficacy.judgement: Scored same on the primary endpoint (PFS HR 0.60 vs placebo). Two linifanib CRC trials are recorded but not scored: O'Neil 2014 tested superiority over bevacizumab plus mFOLFOX6 (PFS HR 1.45 low dose, 1.26 high dose), a comparison the xenograft never made, as the KDR sibling tile treats BATON-CRC; Chan 2017 was a single-arm KRAS-mutant trial whose ORR gate (0/30) is not the xenograft's growth-inhibition prediction (63.5% stable disease, PFS 4.7 months). outcome_tested null: the OS phase 3 FACT (NCT02390947, 543 patients, completed Feb 2019) has no results anywhere I could find, as has donafenib's placebo-controlled OS phase 3 (NCT02870582, 536 patients, completed Apr 2020); six and five years of silence are suggestive but not a source. A checker who scores Chan 2017 as a failed primary endpoint would turn this track contra.
efficacy.model: Human tumour cell-line xenografts in mice incl. colon carcinoma (ABT-869/linifanib)
efficacy.note: Famitinib vs placebo in refractory mCRC met its PFS primary endpoint (2.8 vs 1.5 months, HR 0.60), the activity the class's colon xenografts predicted; OS was null and the phase 3 is unreported.
efficacy.quote: The median PFS was 2.8 and 1.5 months in the famitinib and placebo groups (hazard ratio = 0.60, 95% confidence interval = 0.41-0.86, P = 0.004).

patient_trials.quote: The median OS of the famitinib and placebo groups was 7.4 and 7.2 months (P = 0.657).

No statistically significant differences in PFS occurred between bevacizumab and linifanib doses (low, hazard ratio [HR], 1.453 [95% confidence interval [CI], 0.830-2.539]; high, HR, 1.257 [95% CI, 0.672-2.351]).
Although no responses were observed, 63.5% of patients achieved stable disease.
A Multicenter，Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Trial of Famitinib in Patients With Advanced Colorectal Adenocarcinoma
OS is defined as the time from date of randomization to death due to any cause.
Donafenib Monotherapy for Previously Treated Metastatic Colorectal Cancer: Multicentre, Open-label,Phase 1B Safety Study

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. This is a safety-pharmacology model, not the GLP toxicology package: no member's rat/dog/monkey toxicology is public (no FDA review; NMPA reviews unpublished), so that package cannot be opened as a track.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at first public use. The model carries two predictions: VEGFR-TKI hypertension in conscious telemetered rats and mice, and its reversal by ACE inhibitors without loss of antitumour effect (the second never tested in CRC patients).
safety.model: Conscious telemetered rats and SCID mice: linifanib-induced hypertension and its antihypertensive reversal
safety.note: Linifanib raised blood pressure in telemetered rats; ACE inhibitors prevented it without blunting tumour growth inhibition in mice; no CRC patient comparison yet.
safety.quote: We report that ABT-869-induced hypertension can be prevented and reversed with subtherapeutic or therapeutic doses of antihypertensive drugs with a general rank order of ACEi > ARB > CCB.

safety.magnitude_basis: rat blood-pressure rise vs grade 3 hypertension in at least 2 of 30 linifanib CRC patients; no dose margin stated on either side
safety.population: KRAS-mutant, refractory mCRC (30 patients, linifanib 17.5 mg)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Chan 2017; the registry results (posted 2014-08-26) do not itemise hypertension. The comparison was public earlier in a mixed population (Wong 2009: grade 3 hypertension was dose-limiting at 0.25 and 0.3 mg/kg/d) but this entry is dated to the first CRC-only report to avoid an import. Famitinib agrees (Xu 2017: grade 3-4 hypertension 11.1% in mCRC).
safety.judgement: Predicted harm held in patients: same, direction only. Hand-foot syndrome, proteinuria, thrombocytopenia and hypothyroidism were not predicted by this model, but a telemetry study is not a system that could show them, so its silence is not a miss; the GLP toxicology that could have is not public for any member and is left unscored.
safety.model: Conscious telemetered rats and SCID mice: linifanib-induced hypertension and its antihypertensive reversal
safety.note: Grade 3 hypertension was among the commonest linifanib toxicities in KRAS-mutant mCRC, as rat telemetry predicted; famitinib mCRC patients showed 11.1% grade 3-4 hypertension.
safety.short: Hypertension in patients as rats predicted
safety.quote: Grade 3 treatment-related toxicities occurring in at least two patients were fatigue, hypertension, proteinuria, diarrhea, nausea, oral pain, vomiting, thrombocytopenia, and arthralgia.
safety.reason: Predicted hypertension held in CRC patients
